summary: Standards-axis review of #981 (packages/runtime/src/workRoutes.ts, apps/web/lib/work/api.ts and siblings) and #980 (packages/runtime/tests/work-journal-serve.mjs, trade-invoice-e2e.mjs). Commit hygiene, wire-compatibility discipline and documentation are unusually careful: the LEGACY_BODIES compatibility census, the byte-identical-gate convention deliberately kept across e2e siblings, the vacuity controls for #980s test-only deliverable, and correct Co-Authored-By plus ticket-naming on every commit. Two real standards gaps found. First, #981s build violates the binding WORK-ORDER rule 4 and tdd SKILL.md horizontal-slicing anti-pattern in terms the commit message itself uses: commit ba4071de batches roughly nine ordinary behavioral test cases, beyond the LEGACY_BODIES census pair which plausibly qualifies for the WORK-ORDERs own structural-cell exemption, across two files before any implementation exists, and the very next commit (eb542765) implements the whole carrier feature at once to turn them all green. Second, apps/web/README.md and packages/runtime/README.mds new #981 sections assert the carrier rides on EVERY refusal arm and on every 400 and 409, but restateWorks not_restatable and already_superseded 409 arm never reads carrier(body) and has no detail field on its result type, so the doors typed detail (including superseded_by, which workRoutes.tss answer() already attaches on that exact body) is silently dropped on that one arm, and it is untested and undocumented as an exception. A minor process gap: the lanes final report has no explicit Seams section as WORK-ORDER rule 4 asks for. No mocking, tautology or implementation-coupling violations were found in the new or changed tests; the direct-DB-row assertions in the e2e legs match this repos own established prestate-pin and tail-assertion convention for World e2e tests, so they are not flagged as reaching a side channel.

findings.title: Commit ba4071de batches a whole battery of red tests before any implementation exists, the horizontal-slicing anti-pattern WORK-ORDER rule 4 and tdd/SKILL.md name and forbid
findings.evidence: Commit ba4071de, test(runtime,web): #981 the generic structured-detail carrier, red first, adds in ONE commit, before workRoutes.ts's refusalDetail()/answer() carrier exists at all: packages/runtime/tests/work-routes-unit.test.mjs gains 7 new test() blocks. Two of them (981.route: the carrier is ADDITIVE and 981.route: the door's typed detail rides back VERBATIM) form the LEGACY_BODIES compatibility census, a plausible catalog census structural cell under the WORK-ORDER's own exemption. The other five are ordinary independent behavioral tests with no census shape: 981.route: a detail key never seen before reaches the wire with NO new fold; 981.route: the three constraint folds are the only typing left...; 981.route: party_ambiguous rides the SHARED responder...; 981.route: a detail that is not a typed object carries NO carrier...; 981.route: 403 and 404 stay OPAQUE.... The SAME commit adds 4 more independent test() blocks to apps/web/lib/work/api.test.ts: a 400 with NO structured detail...; a detail key this file has never heard of...; the trade invoice's candidates are the SAME carrier...; an UNNAMED 409 keeps the door's own reason.... The commit message self-describes this as Eight new cells across the two readers of a durable-Work refusal body, written before the carrier exists. The very next commit, eb542765, feat(runtime,web): #981 one structured-detail carrier, and the folds it retires, implements refusalDetail(), answer(), TRADE_INVOICE_FIELD_DEFAULTS and CONSTRAINT_FOLD_REASONS all at once to turn every one of them green. WORK-ORDER.md rule 4 states verbatim: a commit that adds a whole battery of red cells before any implementation is that anti-pattern. .claude/skills/tdd/SKILL.md's Horizontal slicing anti-pattern: writing all tests first, then all implementation... Work in vertical slices instead: one test, one implementation, repeat.
findings.required_fix: No retroactive fix needed on the resulting code: the tests are not tautological and not implementation-coupled, and the feature is correctly built, so this is a process finding against a binding rule rather than a functional defect. Going forward: outside the LEGACY_BODIES census pair, interleave one new behavioral cell at a time with the minimal code that turns it green, rather than landing the whole test battery ahead of the feature commit.

findings.title: New module docs claim the carrier reaches EVERY refusal arm; restateWork's not_restatable/already_superseded 409 arm silently drops it
findings.evidence: apps/web/README.md's new section, #981, the durable-Work refusal carrier, read once, says the carrier surfaces on EVERY refusal arm a durable-Work door can answer with, and names retryWork, cancelWork and takeOverWork explicitly as covered. packages/runtime/README.md's new section says the door's detail rides back whole, under detail, on every 400 and 409 this file builds, naming 403 and 404 as the only deliberate exceptions. But apps/web/lib/work/api.ts's restateWork reads: if (reason is not_restatable or already_superseded or not_restatable_purpose) return kind: not_restatable, reason, status: str(body.status) -- with no spread of carrier(body), and RestateWorkResult's not_restatable arm type has only reason and status, no optional detail field at all, unlike every sibling 400/409 kind in the same file. workRoutes.ts's matching arm DOES attach the carrier: it returns answer(409, { error: reason, reason, status, superseded_by }), and answer() assigns body.detail whenever detail is not null. So the runtime sends the carrier on this exact body and the web client throws it away. No cell in apps/web/lib/work/api.test.ts exercises restateWork's carrier behavior at all -- a search for restateWork in that file returns nothing -- so the gap is untested as well as undocumented.
findings.required_fix: Either add the carrier spread and an optional detail field to RestateWorkResult's not_restatable arm, matching every sibling arm, or narrow the two README claims to name this arm as a second deliberate exception beside 403/404. Add a cell to apps/web/lib/work/api.test.ts exercising restateWork's 409 carrier behavior either way.

findings.title: The lane's final report has no explicit Seams section, as WORK-ORDER rule 4 asks for
findings.evidence: docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/WORK-ORDER.md rule 4 says the seams are the public interfaces the ticket's brief names, and to write them down at the top of the report before testing. docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/reports/wave1-lane10-final.md has no section or heading naming the seams -- a search for the word seam over that file and wave1-lane10-fixround-1.md returns nothing. The seams (workErrorResponse, apps/web/lib/work/api.ts's exported functions, the work-journal-serve.mjs script selector) are only inferable from the per-AC evidence table further down the report.
findings.required_fix: Add an explicit Seams line near the top of the final report naming the public interfaces under test, for this and future lane reports, per WORK-ORDER rule 4.
